transcript: The week after I graduated from university I set off alone for southern Europe But she bare-lined ticket and a worn-out backpack were all I had The old quarter of Barcelona was a maze of bare stone walls and narrow lanes My footsteps echoed against the walls At every turn a small craft shop Or a folk music bar appeared down at the harbour A dozen fishing boats were lined up In the market, the scent of fresh bread and the aroma of rich spices drifted in the air and stirred my appetite. I took a train south and stayed at an inn in a whitewashed village. The owners were a generous elderly couple who served me dinner The furniture was old, but well-kept On the last morning I leaned on the balcony And looked out at the sea The wind blew gently This time of leisure was exactly what I had been seeking On the journey The trip taught me something The world is far more friendly and far broader than I had ever imagined
